source.text: Ἐὰν δὲ ἁμαρτήσῃ εἰς σὲ ὁ ἀδελφός σου, ὕπαγε ἔλεγξον αὐτὸν μεταξὺ σοῦ καὶ αὐτοῦ μόνου.

records.literal_gloss: If but sins against you the brother of you, go reprove him between you and him alone.

en.L: And if {{gender:your brother or sister|your brother}} sins against you, go, show {{gender:them|him}} [the] fault between you and {{gender:them|him}} alone.
en.B: If {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}} sins against you, go and confront {{gender:them|him}} about it, with only the two of you present.
en.R: If {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}} in God's family sins against you, go and talk to {{gender:them|him}} alone. Show {{gender:them|him}} what {{gender:they|he}} did wrong.

fr.L: Et si {{gender:ton frère ou ta sœur|ton frère}} pèche contre toi, va, montre-lui sa faute entre vous deux seulement.
fr.B: Si {{gender:un frère ou une sœur|ton frère}} pèche contre toi, va lui parler franchement de sa faute, seul à seul.
fr.R: Si {{gender:un frère ou une sœur|ton frère}} de la famille de Dieu pèche contre toi, va lui parler seul à seul. Montre-lui ce qu’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} a fait de mal.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow member of the community of disciples, man or woman
decisions.reason: As in 5:22-24 and 12:49-50, a brother is one who belongs to Jesus's family of disciples. The teaching applies to women as well as men.

decisions.choice: sins against you, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: sins, without "against you", the reading of some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some important early manuscripts lack "against you". Without it, the teaching covers any sin of a fellow disciple, not only a wrong done to you. The words may have been added from 18:21, or dropped by a copyist. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: show the fault: bring the wrong into the open so that it is admitted
decisions.reason: The verb means to expose or convince. The aim is to win the person back (18:15), as in Leviticus 19:17.

decisions.choice: Leviticus 19:17: rebuke your neighbor, and do not hate him
decisions.reason: The law told Israel to correct a neighbor openly rather than nurse hatred in the heart.

decisions.choice: {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The teaching covers women and men, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: in God's family
decisions.reason: Readable says that a fellow believer is meant.

decisions.choice: {{gender:ton frère ou ta sœur|ton frère}}, with {{gender:il ou elle|il}} for the subject pronoun; "lui" with no span (for 18:15-35)
decisions.reason: As Luke 17:3: the brother is any fellow disciple, man or woman (m1). The subject pronoun that agrees with the noun goes under the same setting; the object pronoun "lui" serves either sex, so it takes none. Where the English has "between you and {{gender:them|him}} alone", French says "entre vous deux seulement" (L) and "seul à seul" (B, R), which need no setting.

source.text: ἐάν σου ἀκούσῃ, ἐκέρδησας τὸν ἀδελφόν σου·

records.literal_gloss: If you he hears, you have gained the brother of you;

en.L: If {{gender:they|he}} will listen to you, you have gained {{gender:your brother or sister|your brother}};
en.B: If {{gender:they|he}} will listen to you, you have won {{gender:your brother or sister|your brother}} back.
en.R: Maybe {{gender:they|he}} will listen to you. Then you have won {{gender:your brother or sister|your brother}} back.

fr.L: S’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} t’écoute, tu as gagné {{gender:ton frère ou ta sœur|ton frère}} ;
fr.B: S’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} t’écoute, tu auras regagné {{gender:ton frère ou ta sœur|ton frère}}.
fr.R: Peut-être qu’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} t’écoutera. Alors tu auras retrouvé {{gender:ton frère ou ta sœur|ton frère}}.

decisions.choice: gained: won back to God and to the community
decisions.reason: The verb is a word from trade. Here what is gained is the person, brought back from the path of sin, like the sheep in 18:13.

decisions.choice: listen: heed, accept the correction
decisions.reason: To listen here is to take the correction to heart and put the wrong right.

decisions.choice: will listen
decisions.reason: The helping verb lets the gender setting change the pronoun without changing the verb.

decisions.choice: won back
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the gain is.

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀκούσῃ, παράλαβε μετὰ σοῦ ἔτι ἕνα ἢ δύο, ἵνα ἐπὶ στόματος δύο μαρτύρων ἢ τριῶν σταθῇ πᾶν ῥῆμα·

records.literal_gloss: If but not he hears, take with you yet one or two, that on mouth of two witnesses or three may be established every word;

en.L: But if {{gender:they|he}} will not listen, take one or two more with you, so that 'by [the] mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.'
en.B: If {{gender:they|he}} still will not listen, go back with one or two others, so that 'every charge may be settled on the word of two or three witnesses.'
en.R: If {{gender:they|he}} will still not listen, take one or two other people with you. The Scriptures say, 'Every charge must be proved by two or three witnesses.'

fr.L: Mais s’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} n’écoute pas, prends avec toi encore une ou deux [personnes], afin que “sur la bouche de deux ou trois témoins toute parole soit établie”.
fr.B: S’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} refuse encore d’écouter, retournes-y avec une ou deux autres personnes, afin que “toute affaire soit réglée sur la parole de deux ou trois témoins”.
fr.R: S’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} ne veut toujours pas écouter, emmène avec toi une ou deux autres personnes. Les Écritures disent : “Toute accusation doit être prouvée par deux ou trois témoins.”

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 19:15: two or three witnesses
decisions.reason: The law said that a charge must be confirmed by two or three witnesses. Paul uses the same rule in 2 Corinthians 13:1.

decisions.choice: every word: every matter, every charge
decisions.reason: Like the Hebrew word it follows, the word can mean a matter or case as well as a word.

decisions.choice: so that: the others confirm what is said and help win the person
alternatives: the others serve only as a court
decisions.reason: The witnesses make sure the matter is fairly heard. They may also add their voice to the call to put things right.

decisions.choice: The Scriptures say
decisions.reason: Readable says that the words come from the law.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: As in 18:15.

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ παρακούσῃ αὐτῶν, εἰπὸν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ· ἐὰν δὲ καὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας παρακούσῃ, ἔστω σοι ὥσπερ ὁ ἐθνικὸς καὶ ὁ τελώνης.

records.literal_gloss: If but he refuses to hear them, tell to the church; if but also the church he refuses to hear, let him be to you as the Gentile and the tax collector.

en.L: And if {{gender:they|he}} will not heed them, tell [it] to the church; and if {{gender:they|he}} will not heed even the church, let {{gender:them|him}} be to you like the Gentile and the tax collector.
en.B: If {{gender:they|he}} will not hear them either, bring the matter before the church. And if {{gender:they|he}} will not hear the church either, regard {{gender:them|him}} as an outsider, like a Gentile or a tax collector.
en.R: If {{gender:they|he}} will not listen to them, tell the whole church. If {{gender:they|he}} will not listen even to the church, treat {{gender:them|him}} like someone who does not know God, or like a tax collector.

fr.L: Et s’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} refuse de les écouter, dis-le à l’église ; et s’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} refuse d’écouter même l’église, qu’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} soit pour toi comme le païen et le collecteur d’impôts.
fr.B: S’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} ne les écoute pas non plus, porte l’affaire devant l’église. Et s’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} n’écoute pas non plus l’église, considère qu’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} ne fait plus partie des vôtres, comme un païen ou un collecteur d’impôts.
fr.R: S’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} ne les écoute pas, dis-le à toute l’église. Et s’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} n’écoute même pas l’église, alors, pour toi, {{gender:il ou elle|il}} sera comme quelqu’un qui ne connaît pas Dieu, ou comme un collecteur d’impôts.

decisions.choice: the church: the gathered community of Jesus's disciples
decisions.reason: The word means an assembly. Jesus used it in 16:18 of the community he would build; here it is the local gathering of believers.

decisions.choice: the Gentile and the tax collector: people outside the fellowship
decisions.reason: Jews of the time kept apart from Gentiles and tax collectors at table (9:11). The one who will not repent is to be treated as outside the community. Yet Jesus himself sought out tax collectors (9:9-13; 11:19), and the parable of the sheep goes before these words.

decisions.choice: the Gentile: one outside Israel who did not worship its God
alternatives: a foreigner in a neutral sense
decisions.reason: As in 5:47 and 6:7.

decisions.choice: an outsider
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the comparison means, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: someone who does not know God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as in 5:47.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they|he}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: As in 18:15.

decisions.choice: l’église, lowercase
decisions.reason: The style guide writes "l’église" for one gathered community and "l’Église" for the whole body of believers. Here the disciples who know the offender are meant, gathered to hear the matter (m1), so the lowercase form fits.

decisions.choice: le païen (L), un païen (B); quelqu’un qui ne connaît pas Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: The word is an adjective for one of the nations who did not worship Israel's God (m3), and the point is that such a person stood outside the fellowship (m2). French "païen" says exactly that; "non-Juif", the style guide's word for the plural noun "Gentiles", would make the point one of birth rather than worship.

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅσα ἐὰν δήσητε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται δεδεμένα ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ὅσα ἐὰν λύσητε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται λελυμένα ἐν οὐρανῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you, as many as if you bind on the earth will be having been bound in heaven, and as many as if you loose on the earth will be having been loosed in heaven.

en.L: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will have been loosed in heaven.
en.B: Truly I tell you, what you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and what you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.
en.R: I tell you the truth, whatever you forbid on earth will be forbidden in heaven. And whatever you allow on earth will be allowed in heaven.

fr.L: En vérité, je vous le dis, tout ce que vous lierez sur la terre aura été lié dans le ciel, et tout ce que vous délierez sur la terre aura été délié dans le ciel.
fr.B: En vérité, je vous le dis, ce que vous lierez sur la terre sera lié dans le ciel, et ce que vous délierez sur la terre sera délié dans le ciel.
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : tout ce que vous interdirez sur la terre sera interdit dans le ciel. Et tout ce que vous permettrez sur la terre sera permis dans le ciel.

decisions.choice: bind and loose: decide what is forbidden and what is allowed, and so whom to hold to their sin and whom to set free
decisions.reason: Jewish teachers spoke of binding and loosing when they ruled what the law forbade or allowed. Here, after 18:15-17, it covers the church's judgment on a member who sins. Compare 16:19 and John 20:23.

decisions.choice: will have been bound: heaven's verdict stands with the church's
alternatives: heaven will afterward agree with whatever the church decides
decisions.reason: The form is a future perfect. It may mean that the church's decision follows what God has already decided, or simply that God will confirm it. The grammar does not settle the order.

decisions.choice: you: the plural, the disciples together
decisions.reason: In 16:19 the same promise is made to Peter. Here the "you" is plural, and the church of 18:17 is in view.

decisions.choice: will be bound; will be loosed, as at 16:19
alternatives: will stand bound; will stand free
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the same words as at 16:19, so readers can see it is the same promise, now given to all the disciples. Literal keeps the future perfect form.

decisions.choice: forbid; allow
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom, following the meaning decision.

source.text: Πάλιν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν δύο συμφωνήσωσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς περὶ παντὸς πράγματος οὗ ἐὰν αἰτήσωνται, γενήσεται αὐτοῖς παρὰ τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Again truly I say to you that if two agree of you on the earth about any matter which if they ask, it will be done for them by the Father of me the in heavens.

en.L: Again, truly I tell you that if two of you agree on earth about any matter that they ask, it will be done for them by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father who [is] in [the] heavens.
en.B: And again, truly I tell you: if two of you here on earth are of one mind about anything they ask for, it will be done for them by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven.
en.R: I tell you the truth again. Suppose two of you here on earth agree about something and ask God for it. Then {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven will do it for them.

fr.L: De nouveau, en vérité, je vous dis que si deux d’entre vous s’accordent sur la terre au sujet de toute chose qu’ils demanderont, cela leur sera fait par {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui [est] dans les cieux.
fr.B: Je vous le dis encore, en vérité : si deux d’entre vous, ici sur la terre, sont d’accord pour demander quoi que ce soit, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui est dans le ciel le leur accordera.
fr.R: Je vous le dis encore, c’est la vérité : imaginez que deux d’entre vous, ici sur la terre, soient d’accord pour demander quelque chose à Dieu. Alors {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui est au ciel le fera pour eux.

decisions.choice: any matter: anything they ask, including the cases the church must judge
decisions.reason: The word can mean a legal case (1 Corinthians 6:1), which fits the setting of 18:15-18. But the promise is put broadly, about anything asked.

decisions.choice: agree: be of one mind, in harmony
decisions.reason: The verb means to sound together. The disciples ask God together, in agreement.

decisions.choice: ask God for it
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom they ask.

source.text: οὗ γάρ εἰσιν δύο ἢ τρεῖς συνηγμένοι εἰς τὸ ἐμὸν ὄνομα, ἐκεῖ εἰμι ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Where for are two or three gathered into the my name, there I am in midst of them.

en.L: For where two or three are gathered in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, there I am in [the] middle of them."
en.B: For whenever two or three come together in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, I am there among them."
en.R: When two or three people meet together because they follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I am there with them."

fr.L: Car là où deux ou trois sont rassemblés en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, je suis là au milieu d’eux. »
fr.B: Car chaque fois que deux ou trois se réunissent en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, je suis là, parmi eux. »
fr.R: Quand deux ou trois personnes se réunissent parce qu’elles {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suivent, je suis là avec elles. »

decisions.choice: gathered in my name: meeting as those who belong to me
alternatives: meeting while saying my name aloud
decisions.reason: As in 18:5, "in my name" names the bond with Jesus. They meet as his disciples.

decisions.choice: I am there among them: the promise of Jesus's presence
decisions.reason: Matthew opens with "God with us" (1:23) and closes with "I am with you always" (28:20). Jesus promises to be with even the smallest gathering of his disciples.

decisions.choice: for: the reason the Father hears the two
decisions.reason: The Father answers their prayer because Jesus is present with those who meet in his name.

decisions.choice: because they follow me
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in my name" means here.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: Peter's question in 18:21 breaks into the speech, so the quotation closes here and reopens at 18:22.

source.text: Τότε προσελθὼν αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν· Κύριε, ποσάκις ἁμαρτήσει εἰς ἐμὲ ὁ ἀδελφός μου καὶ ἀφήσω αὐτῷ;

records.literal_gloss: Then having come to him the Peter said, Lord, how often will sin against me the brother of me and I will forgive him?

en.L: Then Peter came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Lord, how many times will {{gender:my brother or sister|my brother}} sin against me and I forgive {{gender:them|him}}?
en.B: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, "Lord, if {{gender:a brother or sister|my brother}} keeps on sinning against me, how many times must I forgive?
en.R: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, "Lord, suppose {{gender:a brother or sister|my brother}} in God's family sins against me again and again. How many times should I forgive {{gender:them|him}}?

fr.L: Alors Pierre, s’étant approché, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Seigneur, combien de fois, si {{gender:mon frère ou ma sœur|mon frère}} pèche contre moi, lui pardonnerai-je ?
fr.B: Alors Pierre vint trouver Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demanda : « Seigneur, si {{gender:un frère ou une sœur|mon frère}} ne cesse de pécher contre moi, combien de fois dois-je pardonner ?
fr.R: Alors Pierre est venu voir Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a demandé : « Seigneur, imagine qu’{{gender:un frère ou une sœur|un frère}} de la famille de Dieu pèche contre moi encore et encore. Combien de fois est-ce que je dois lui pardonner ?

decisions.choice: how many times: how often must I forgive the same person
decisions.reason: Peter asks about one person who sins against him again and again. He takes up the brother of 18:15.

decisions.choice: my brother: a fellow disciple, man or woman
decisions.reason: As in 18:15.

decisions.choice: forgive: let go of the wrong and not hold it against the person
decisions.reason: The verb means to release or let go, the word used of debts in 6:12 and 18:27.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:a brother or sister|my brother}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: As in 18:15, the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 18:21
alternatives: closing the quotation at the end of this sentence
decisions.reason: Peter's question runs over two sentences.

decisions.choice: combien de fois, si {{gender:mon frère ou ma sœur|mon frère}} pèche contre moi, lui pardonnerai-je ?
alternatives: combien de fois {{gender:mon frère ou ma sœur|mon frère}} péchera-t-{{gender:il ou elle|il}} contre moi
decisions.reason: The Greek joins two futures with "and". French inversion would put the gender span inside "péchera-t-il", which cannot read naturally as "il ou elle", so Literal turns the first verb into a condition and keeps the question on forgiving.

source.text: ἕως ἑπτάκις;

records.literal_gloss: Up to seven times?

en.L: Up to seven times?"
en.B: As many as seven times?"
en.R: Should I forgive seven times?"

fr.L: Jusqu’à sept fois ? »
fr.B: Aller jusqu’à sept fois ? »
fr.R: Est-ce que je dois pardonner sept fois ? »

decisions.choice: seven times: a generous number
decisions.reason: Seven is the number of fullness. Peter offers more than would usually be expected (compare Luke 17:4).

decisions.choice: Should I forgive
decisions.reason: Readable makes the short question a full sentence.

source.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐ λέγω σοι ἕως ἑπτάκις ἀλλὰ ἕως ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά.

records.literal_gloss: Says to him the Jesus, Not I say to you up to seven times but up to seventy times seven.

en.L: Jesus says to him, "I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy-seven times.
en.B: Jesus told him, "Not just up to seven times, but up to seventy-seven times.
en.R: Jesus answered, "I tell you, not only seven times. You must forgive seventy-seven times.

fr.L: Jésus lui dit : « Je ne te dis pas jusqu’à sept fois, mais jusqu’à soixante-dix-sept fois.
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « Pas seulement jusqu’à sept fois, mais jusqu’à soixante-dix-sept fois.
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Je te le dis : pas seulement sept fois. Tu dois pardonner soixante-dix-sept fois.

decisions.choice: seventy-seven times
alternatives: seventy times seven, that is, four hundred and ninety times
decisions.reason: The Greek words can be read either way. The same words stand in the Greek Old Testament for Lamech's "seventy-seven times" in Genesis 4:24, which suggests that sense. Either way, Jesus means there is to be no limit.

decisions.choice: Genesis 4:24: Lamech's boast of revenge seventy-seven times
decisions.reason: Lamech boasted that he would be avenged seventy-seven times. Jesus turns the number of unlimited revenge into a number of unlimited forgiveness.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 18:35
alternatives: closing the quotation at the end of this sentence
decisions.reason: Jesus's answer goes on into the parable of 18:23-35, which is one speech.

decisions.choice: You must forgive
decisions.reason: Readable makes the answer a full sentence.

source.text: Διὰ τοῦτο ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ ὃς ἠθέλησεν συνᾶραι λόγον μετὰ τῶν δούλων αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: Because of this has been likened the kingdom of the heavens to a man a king who wanted to settle account with the slaves of him;

en.L: Because of this, the kingdom of the heavens has been compared to a man, a king, who wanted to settle accounts with his slaves.
en.B: That is why the kingdom of heaven is like this: a king decided it was time to go over the accounts of his servants.
en.R: So this is what the kingdom of heaven is like. There was a king who decided to have his servants settle what they owed him.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi le royaume des cieux a été comparé à un homme, un roi, qui a voulu régler ses comptes avec ses esclaves.
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi le royaume des cieux ressemble à ceci : un roi a décidé qu’il était temps de vérifier les comptes de ses serviteurs.
fr.R: Alors voici à quoi ressemble le royaume des cieux. Il y avait un roi qui a décidé de faire payer à ses serviteurs ce qu’ils lui devaient.

decisions.choice: because of this: the parable shows why forgiveness has no limit
alternatives: a loose link with no reason given
decisions.reason: The story explains the answer to Peter: those whom God has forgiven so much must forgive others.

decisions.choice: slaves: royal slaves, who might hold high office
decisions.reason: A king's slaves could manage large sums for him, such as the taxes of a province. They were still his property and answered to him. The word is the one for a slave.

decisions.choice: has been compared: the kingdom is like the whole story
alternatives: the kingdom is like the king himself
decisions.reason: As in 13:24, the comparison is with what happens in the story, not only with its first figure.

decisions.choice: a king, with no deity_pronoun span for him in the story
decisions.reason: The king is a figure in a parable, so the pronouns for him take no span, though he stands for God (18:35).

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: the parable in the passé composé at every level ("a voulu", "a ordonné"); the Greek present of 18:32 kept at Literal ("lui dit")
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: As the style guide settles for the New Testament (Mark 4, Luke 15): the story is part of Jesus's speech, and French tells a story in speech in the passé composé.

decisions.choice: esclaves (L); serviteurs (B, R); compagnon d’esclavage (L), compagnon de service (B) for the fellow slave
decisions.reason: The style guide's forms, as the English: Literal keeps "esclave" and Balanced and Readable say "serviteur"; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that they were owned, and Readable says "vendu comme esclave" in 18:25, where being sold is the point. "Compagnon d’esclavage" is the Literal form of Colossians 1:7.

source.text: ἀρξαμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ συναίρειν προσηνέχθη αὐτῷ εἷς ὀφειλέτης μυρίων ταλάντων.

records.literal_gloss: Having begun and he to settle was brought to him one debtor of ten thousand talents.

en.L: And when he had begun to settle, one was brought to him who was a debtor of ten thousand talents.
en.B: As he began, a man was brought before him who owed him {{units:a sum no worker could earn in a hundred thousand years|ten thousand talents}}.
en.R: As he began, a servant was brought to him who owed him {{units:a sum no worker could earn in a hundred thousand years|ten thousand talents}}. No one could ever pay back that much money.

fr.L: Et quand il a commencé à régler [les comptes], on lui en a amené un qui était débiteur de dix mille talents.
fr.B: Comme il commençait, on lui a amené un homme qui lui devait {{units:une somme qu’aucun ouvrier ne pourrait gagner en cent mille ans|dix mille talents}}.
fr.R: Au début, on lui a amené un serviteur qui lui devait {{units:une somme qu’aucun ouvrier ne pourrait gagner en cent mille ans|dix mille talents}}. Personne n’aurait jamais pu rembourser autant d’argent.

decisions.choice: ten thousand talents: a sum beyond counting
decisions.reason: A talent was a weight of silver worth about six thousand denarii, and a denarius was a laborer's pay for a day (20:2). Ten thousand talents was about sixty million days' wages, more than a laborer could earn in many lifetimes. Ten thousand was the largest number in common Greek use.

decisions.choice: was brought: he was made to come, perhaps under guard
decisions.reason: The passive suggests he did not come willingly.

decisions.choice: {{units:a sum no worker could earn in a hundred thousand years|ten thousand talents}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give a modern figure by default, with the original sum as the alternative. Literal keeps the talents.

decisions.choice: No one could ever pay back that much money.
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sum meant to the hearers.

source.text: μὴ ἔχοντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀποδοῦναι ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος πραθῆναι καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ τὰ τέκνα καὶ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει καὶ ἀποδοθῆναι.

records.literal_gloss: Not having but he to pay, commanded him the master to be sold and the wife and the children and all as much as he has, and to be paid.

en.L: And since he did not have [the means] to pay, the master ordered him to be sold, and [his] wife and children and everything he had, and payment to be made.
en.B: He had no means of paying, so his master gave orders for him to be sold, together with his wife, his children and all he owned, to pay toward the debt.
en.R: The servant could not pay. So the king ordered that he be sold as a slave, along with his wife and children and everything he owned. The money would go toward paying what he owed.

fr.L: Et comme il n’avait pas [de quoi] rendre, le maître a ordonné qu’il soit vendu, ainsi que [sa] femme, [ses] enfants et tout ce qu’il a, et que le remboursement soit fait.
fr.B: Comme il n’avait pas les moyens de payer, son maître a donné l’ordre de le vendre, avec sa femme, ses enfants et tout ce qu’il possédait, pour rembourser une partie de la dette.
fr.R: Le serviteur ne pouvait pas payer. Alors le roi a ordonné qu’on le vende comme esclave, avec sa femme, ses enfants et tout ce qu’il avait. L’argent servirait à payer une partie de ce qu’il devait.

decisions.choice: sold with his family: a debtor and his household could be sold into slavery
alternatives: a punishment the law of Moses required
decisions.reason: Selling a debtor and his family was known in Israel (2 Kings 4:1; Nehemiah 5:5) and across the ancient world. The sale would cover only a tiny part of such a debt.

decisions.choice: the master: the king of 18:23
decisions.reason: The word means lord or master. In the story it is the king, the slave's owner.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable keeps one name for the king throughout the story.

decisions.choice: [the means]; [his]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words English needs.

decisions.choice: sold as a slave
decisions.reason: Readable calls the man "servant" in this parable, as the style guide has it, but keeps "slave" where the king orders him sold with his family: being sold as property is the point here (m1).

source.text: πεσὼν οὖν ὁ δοῦλος προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων· Μακροθύμησον ἐπ’ ἐμοί, καὶ πάντα ἀποδώσω σοι.

records.literal_gloss: Having fallen therefore the slave was bowing down to him saying, Be patient with me, and all I will pay to you.

en.L: So the slave fell down and was bowing before him, saying, 'Be patient with me, and I will pay you everything.'
en.B: At that the servant threw himself to the ground before him and pleaded, 'Give me time, and I will pay back all of it.'
en.R: The servant got down on his knees in front of the king and begged, 'Please be patient with me. I will pay you everything.'

fr.L: Alors l’esclave, s’étant jeté à terre, se prosternait devant lui en disant : “Sois patient envers moi, et je te rendrai tout.”
fr.B: Le serviteur s’est alors jeté à terre devant lui et l’a supplié : “Accorde-moi un délai, et je te rembourserai tout.”
fr.R: Le serviteur s’est mis à genoux devant le roi et l’a supplié : “S’il te plaît, sois patient avec moi. Je te rendrai tout.”

decisions.choice: was bowing: bowing low before a king
decisions.reason: The verb is used for worship and also for bowing low before a ruler, as here. The tense pictures him pleading on and on.

decisions.choice: I will pay you everything: a promise he could never keep
decisions.reason: No slave could repay such a sum (18:24). He asks for time, but the king gives far more.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks
decisions.reason: The slave's words are inside Jesus's speech, so they take inner quotation marks.

decisions.choice: pleaded (B); begged (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how he spoke, as the bowing shows.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: “ ” for words inside Jesus's speech; the servant says "tu" to the king
decisions.reason: French typography nests « » and then “ ”. The style guide uses "tu" for one person, and the servants of the parable say "tu" as people say it to Jesus; "vous" would add a court register the Greek does not mark.

source.text: σπλαγχνισθεὶς δὲ ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἀπέλυσεν αὐτόν, καὶ τὸ δάνειον ἀφῆκεν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Having been moved with compassion and the master of the slave that released him, and the loan forgave him.

en.L: And the master of that slave, moved with compassion, released him and forgave him the loan.
en.B: The master was moved with pity for that servant. He set him free and forgave him the debt.
en.R: The king felt sorry for the servant. So he let him go free and forgave him the whole debt.

fr.L: Et le maître de cet esclave, ému de compassion, l’a relâché et lui a pardonné le prêt.
fr.B: Le maître a été pris de pitié pour ce serviteur. Il l’a laissé partir et lui a pardonné sa dette.
fr.R: Le roi a eu pitié du serviteur. Alors il l’a laissé partir libre et lui a pardonné toute sa dette.

decisions.choice: moved with compassion: deeply moved
decisions.reason: This is the word used of Jesus's compassion for the crowds (9:36; 14:14).

decisions.choice: the loan: the debt, spoken of as money lent
decisions.reason: Whatever the slave had received from the king, the master treats it as a loan and cancels it.

decisions.choice: forgave: the same verb as Peter's question (18:21) and 18:35
decisions.reason: The master does more than the slave asked. He does not give time; he lets the whole debt go.

decisions.choice: forgave
decisions.reason: The same word is kept at every level to tie the story to Peter's question and to 18:35.

decisions.choice: the whole debt
decisions.reason: Readable says that the debt was cancelled in full, as 18:32 says.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: pardonner at every level ("lui a pardonné sa dette"), as in 18:21-22, 18:32, 18:35
decisions.reason: "Remettre une dette" is the usual French idiom, but it would break the link the English keeps with Peter's question and with 18:35 (m3). "Pardonner une dette" is good French and keeps one verb through the passage.

source.text: ἐξελθὼν δὲ ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος εὗρεν ἕνα τῶν συνδούλων αὐτοῦ ὃς ὤφειλεν αὐτῷ ἑκατὸν δηνάρια, καὶ κρατήσας αὐτὸν ἔπνιγεν λέγων· Ἀπόδος εἴ τι ὀφείλεις.

records.literal_gloss: Having gone out but the slave that found one of the fellow slaves of him who owed him a hundred denarii, and having seized him he was choking [him] saying, Pay if anything you owe.

en.L: But that slave went out and found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred denarii, and seizing him, he began to choke [him], saying, 'Pay back whatever you owe.'
en.B: But no sooner had that servant left than he came upon one of his fellow servants who owed him {{units:about a hundred days' wages|a hundred denarii}}. He grabbed him by the throat. 'Pay me what you owe!' he said.
en.R: Then that servant went out and found another servant who owed him {{units:about a hundred days' wages|a hundred denarii}}. He grabbed the man and started choking him. He said, 'Pay back the money you owe me!'

fr.L: Mais cet esclave, étant sorti, a trouvé un de ses compagnons d’esclavage qui lui devait cent deniers, et, l’ayant saisi, il l’étranglait en disant : “Rends ce que tu dois.”
fr.B: Mais à peine sorti, ce serviteur est tombé sur l’un de ses compagnons de service qui lui devait {{units:environ cent journées de salaire|cent deniers}}. Il l’a pris à la gorge. “Paie-moi ce que tu me dois !” lui a-t-il dit.
fr.R: Ensuite, ce serviteur est sorti et il a trouvé un autre serviteur qui lui devait {{units:environ cent journées de salaire|cent deniers}}. Il a attrapé l’homme et s’est mis à l’étrangler. Il lui a dit : “Rends-moi l’argent que tu me dois !”

decisions.choice: a hundred denarii: about a hundred days' wages
decisions.reason: A denarius was a laborer's pay for a day (20:2). A hundred denarii was a real debt, a third of a year's wages, but next to ten thousand talents it was almost nothing.

decisions.choice: pay if you owe anything: pay what you owe
alternatives: a doubt about whether he owes anything
decisions.reason: The "if" does not question the debt. It is a harsh demand for whatever is owed.

decisions.choice: was choking: began to choke him
decisions.reason: The tense pictures the action going on or beginning.

decisions.choice: {{units:about a hundred days' wages|a hundred denarii}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give a modern figure by default, with the original sum as the alternative. Literal keeps the denarii.

decisions.choice: fellow servants (B); another servant (R)
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the man is in the same position as the first, owned by the king, and Literal keeps "fellow slaves".

source.text: πεσὼν οὖν ὁ σύνδουλος αὐτοῦ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν λέγων· Μακροθύμησον ἐπ’ ἐμοί, καὶ ἀποδώσω σοι.

records.literal_gloss: Having fallen therefore the fellow slave of him was begging him saying, Be patient with me, and I will pay you.

en.L: So his fellow slave fell down and was begging him, saying, 'Be patient with me, and I will pay you.'
en.B: His fellow servant dropped to the ground and pleaded with him, 'Give me time, and I will pay you back.'
en.R: The other servant got down on his knees and begged him, 'Please be patient with me. I will pay you back.'

fr.L: Alors son compagnon d’esclavage, s’étant jeté à terre, le suppliait en disant : “Sois patient envers moi, et je te rendrai.”
fr.B: Son compagnon de service s’est jeté à terre et l’a supplié : “Accorde-moi un délai, et je te rembourserai.”
fr.R: L’autre serviteur s’est mis à genoux et l’a supplié : “S’il te plaît, sois patient avec moi. Je te rendrai l’argent.”

decisions.choice: the same plea as 18:26
decisions.reason: The words are almost those the first slave used to the king, and this debt could in fact be repaid. The echo makes the first slave's refusal plain.

decisions.choice: fell down, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: fell down at his feet, and "I will pay you everything", the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "at his feet" and "everything", making the plea match 18:26 more closely. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the same words as 18:26 at each level
decisions.reason: The echo is kept so that readers hear the same plea.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἤθελεν, ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν ἔβαλεν αὐτὸν εἰς φυλακὴν ἕως οὗ ἀποδῷ τὸ ὀφειλόμενον.

records.literal_gloss: He but not was willing, but having gone away he threw him into prison until he should pay the being owed.

en.L: But he was not willing; instead he went and threw him into prison until he should pay what was owed.
en.B: But he would not hear of it. He went off and had the man put in prison until the debt was paid.
en.R: But the first servant would not wait. He had the other man thrown into prison. He would stay there until he paid back what he owed.

fr.L: Mais lui ne voulait pas ; au contraire, il est allé le jeter en prison jusqu’à ce qu’il ait payé ce qui était dû.
fr.B: Mais il n’a rien voulu entendre. Il est parti et a fait mettre l’homme en prison jusqu’à ce que la dette soit payée.
fr.R: Mais le premier serviteur n’a pas voulu attendre. Il a fait jeter l’autre homme en prison. Celui-ci devait y rester jusqu’à ce qu’il ait rendu ce qu’il devait.

decisions.choice: prison until he should pay: prison for debt
decisions.reason: As in 5:25-26, a debtor could be held until the debt was paid, often by his family or friends.

decisions.choice: threw him into prison: by legal means, as a creditor could
decisions.reason: The slave would have had the man put in prison through the officials. The wording stresses his harshness.

decisions.choice: had the man put (B); had the other man thrown (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that he did this through others, following the meaning decision.

source.text: ἰδόντες οὖν οἱ σύνδουλοι αὐτοῦ τὰ γενόμενα ἐλυπήθησαν σφόδρα, καὶ ἐλθόντες διεσάφησαν τῷ κυρίῳ ἑαυτῶν πάντα τὰ γενόμενα.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen therefore the fellow slaves of him the things having happened they were grieved greatly, and having come they explained to the master of themselves all the things having happened.

en.L: So when his fellow slaves saw what had happened, they were deeply distressed, and they went and reported to their master all that had happened.
en.B: When the other servants saw what had taken place, they were deeply upset. They went to their master and told him the whole story.
en.R: The other servants saw what happened, and it made them very upset. So they went and told the king everything.

fr.L: Ses compagnons d’esclavage, ayant donc vu ce qui était arrivé, ont été profondément attristés, et ils sont allés exposer à leur maître tout ce qui était arrivé.
fr.B: Quand les autres serviteurs ont vu ce qui s’était passé, ils ont été profondément bouleversés. Ils sont allés trouver leur maître et lui ont tout raconté.
fr.R: Les autres serviteurs ont vu ce qui s’était passé, et ils ont été très choqués. Alors ils sont allés tout raconter au roi.

decisions.choice: deeply distressed: grieved and upset
decisions.reason: The verb means to be grieved or pained. They are troubled at the cruelty they have seen.

decisions.choice: reported: explained in full
decisions.reason: The verb means to make clear. They give the master the whole account.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: As in 18:25.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: τότε προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ λέγει αὐτῷ· Δοῦλε πονηρέ, πᾶσαν τὴν ὀφειλὴν ἐκείνην ἀφῆκά σοι, ἐπεὶ παρεκάλεσάς με·

records.literal_gloss: Then having summoned him the master of him says to him, Slave wicked, all the debt that I forgave you, since you begged me;

en.L: Then his master summoned him and says to him, 'Wicked slave! I forgave you all that debt, because you begged me.
en.B: So the master had him called back and said to him, 'Wicked servant! You pleaded with me, and I forgave you the whole of that debt.
en.R: Then the king called the servant in. He said to him, 'You evil servant! You begged me to help you, so I forgave everything you owed me.

fr.L: Alors son maître, l’ayant fait appeler, lui dit : “Méchant esclave ! Toute cette dette, je te l’ai pardonnée, puisque tu m’as supplié.
fr.B: Le maître l’a alors fait rappeler et lui a dit : “Méchant serviteur ! Tu m’as supplié, et je t’ai pardonné toute cette dette.
fr.R: Alors le roi a fait venir le serviteur. Il lui a dit : “Serviteur sans cœur ! Tu m’as supplié de t’aider, alors je t’ai pardonné tout ce que tu me devais.

decisions.choice: wicked: evil, here cruel and without mercy
decisions.reason: The word is the usual one for evil. His wickedness is his hardness toward a fellow slave after he had been shown mercy.

decisions.choice: because you begged me: the debt was forgiven only because he asked
decisions.reason: The slave did nothing to earn it. He only asked, and the king forgave.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: the master's words open here and close at the end of 18:33
alternatives: closing the inner quotation at the end of this sentence
decisions.reason: The master's rebuke runs over two sentences, so the inner quotation stays open.

decisions.choice: to help you
decisions.reason: Readable says what he begged for.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: οὐκ ἔδει καὶ σὲ ἐλεῆσαι τὸν σύνδουλόν σου, ὡς κἀγὼ σὲ ἠλέησα;

records.literal_gloss: Not was it necessary also you to have mercy on the fellow slave of you, as also I you had mercy?

en.L: Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I also had mercy on you?'
en.B: Should you not have shown your fellow servant the same mercy I showed you?'
en.R: You should have shown mercy to the other servant, just as I showed mercy to you.'

fr.L: Ne fallait-il pas que toi aussi tu aies pitié de ton compagnon d’esclavage, comme moi aussi j’ai eu pitié de toi ?”
fr.B: Ne devais-tu pas, toi aussi, avoir pour ton compagnon de service la même pitié que j’ai eue pour toi ?”
fr.R: Tu aurais dû avoir pitié de l’autre serviteur, comme j’ai eu pitié de toi.”

decisions.choice: should you not: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The form expects agreement. He was bound to show the mercy he had received.

decisions.choice: as I had mercy on you: mercy received calls for mercy given
alternatives: mercy as a reward for mercy
decisions.reason: This is the point of the story: those who have been forgiven must forgive. Compare 5:7 and 6:12.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: Should you not have had mercy?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes"; Readable gives the answer.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: καὶ ὀργισθεὶς ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν τοῖς βασανισταῖς ἕως οὗ ἀποδῷ πᾶν τὸ ὀφειλόμενον.

records.literal_gloss: And having been angry the master of him handed over him to the torturers until he should pay all the being owed.

en.L: And in anger his master handed him over to the torturers until he should pay all that was owed.
en.B: Then the master, now angry, gave him over to the torturers, to stay with them until he had repaid the whole debt.
en.R: The king was very angry. He handed the servant over to men who would torture him in prison. He would stay there until he paid back everything he owed.

fr.L: Et son maître, mis en colère, l’a livré aux tortionnaires jusqu’à ce qu’il ait payé tout ce qui était dû.
fr.B: Alors le maître, en colère, l’a livré aux bourreaux, jusqu’à ce qu’il ait remboursé toute la dette.
fr.R: Le roi était très en colère. Il a livré le serviteur à des hommes qui allaient le torturer en prison. Il devait y rester jusqu’à ce qu’il ait rendu tout ce qu’il devait.

decisions.choice: the torturers: jailers who used torture
decisions.reason: The word means those who torture. Torture was sometimes used on prisoners to make them or their families pay.

decisions.choice: until he should pay all: a debt that could never be paid
decisions.reason: The debt was beyond paying (18:24), so the words point to punishment without release. Jesus applies it in 18:35.

decisions.choice: in anger: the king's anger at the slave's cruelty
decisions.reason: The master was angry because the slave had not shown mercy, not because of the money (18:33).

decisions.choice: men who would torture him in prison
decisions.reason: Readable says who the torturers were.

source.text: Οὕτως καὶ ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος ποιήσει ὑμῖν ἐὰν μὴ ἀφῆτε ἕκαστος τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν καρδιῶν ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: So also the Father of me the heavenly will do to you if not you forgive each the brother of him from the hearts of you.

en.L: So also {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heavenly Father will do to you, if you do not each forgive {{gender:your brother or sister|your brother}} from your hearts."
en.B: My Father in heaven will deal with you in the same way if you do not forgive {{gender:your brother or sister|your brother}} from the heart, each one of you."
en.R: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven will do the same to you if you do not truly forgive {{gender:your brother or sister|your brother}} from your heart."

fr.L: C’est ainsi que {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père céleste vous traitera aussi, si vous ne pardonnez pas, chacun, à {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}} du fond de vos cœurs. »
fr.B: Mon Père qui est dans le ciel agira de la même manière envers vous si chacun de vous ne pardonne pas à {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}} du fond du cœur. »
fr.R: Et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui est au ciel vous traitera de la même façon si vous ne pardonnez pas vraiment, du fond du cœur, à {{gender:votre frère ou votre sœur|votre frère}}. »

decisions.choice: so also my Father will do: God will judge the unforgiving
alternatives: God's forgiveness is earned by forgiving others
decisions.reason: As in 6:14-15, forgiveness received and forgiveness given belong together. One who refuses to forgive shows that he has not taken God's mercy to heart.

decisions.choice: from your hearts: truly, from within
decisions.reason: In Scripture the heart is the center of thought and will (5:28). Forgiveness must be real, not only in words.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow disciple, man or woman
{{gender:your brother or sister|your brother}}
decisions.reason: As in 18:15, the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: The speech that began in 18:22 ends here, and with it the fourth long speech in Matthew. 19:1 returns to the story.

decisions.choice: in heaven
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the form of 6:9 and 18:10.
